revision:
ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 pieces, but give white and black pieces unmistakably different fills/outlines while retaining classic glyph silhouettes. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Consolidate the side panel into a continuous hierarchy: title/context, current turn, a clearly bounded move-history table with readable headers and rows, then controls immediately beneath it. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Normalize every piece glyph to a consistent optical bounding box, baseline, stroke/shadow treatment, and contrast strategy; make white and black sets equally crisp rather than stylistically asymmetric. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Develop a distinctive modern-club identity through bespoke piece silhouettes, subtle rank/file ornament, and meaningful turn or last-move emphasis; give the side panel tournament-card details and material indicators that add character without compromising classical legibility. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 pieces, but give white and black pieces unmistakably different fills/outlines while retaining classic glyph silhouettes.—while using the clarity action—Consolidate the side panel into a continuous hierarchy: title/context, current turn, a clearly bounded move-history table with readable headers and rows, then controls immediately beneath it.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Normalize every piece glyph to a consistent optical bounding box, baseline, stroke/shadow treatment, and contrast strategy; make white and black sets equally crisp rather than stylistically asymmetric.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Develop a distinctive modern-club identity through bespoke piece silhouettes, subtle rank/file ornament, and meaningful turn or last-move emphasis; give the side panel tournament-card details and material indicators that add character without compromising classical legibility.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
